page: UpCloud GPU-8xCPU-64GB-1xL4 is a GPU-accelerated server instance designed for workloads requiring dedicated graphics acceleration and balanced system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with x86_64 architecture, the system provides 8 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The instance features 64 GB of system memory, yielding 8 GB of RAM per core, and is backed by the KVM hypervisor. It integrates a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 24 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks reveal exceptional single-core capabilities. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-tier results in single-core stress-ng tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core evaluations, particularly in text processing. Multi-core performance, including multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation, falls into the average tier. The onboard NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers strong performance in image processing and average performance in ray tracing. In language model tasks, the server demonstrates top-tier text generation speeds for small 135M models, though prompt processing speeds remain average.

From a resource density perspective, the server offers a highly specialized hardware profile, balancing a modern Ada Lovelace GPU with a high-performance AMD EPYC CPU. The absence of local storage means users must provision external block storage, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. This configuration is highly cost-efficient for workloads that leverage GPU acceleration without requiring massive multi-core CPU scaling. Appropriate workloads include small-scale machine learning inference, image processing, single-threaded data compression, and general-purpose GPU computing.

Built on the x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization, this instance integrates a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 24 GB of VRAM from the Ada Lovelace family. It does not include local storage, requiring external block storage provisioning. Benchmark data highlights top-tier single-core CPU performance, single-threaded compression, and small-model LLM text generation, while multi-core operations and memory bandwidth perform at average levels. The GPU delivers strong image processing capabilities. This configuration is highly suited for GPU-accelerated workloads, machine learning inference, image processing, and single-core intensive applications.
